newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca continues record run on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca continues record run on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in British pharmaceuticals group Zeneca climbed to record highs on Thursday, gaining over one percent in an otherwise steady market on renewed takeover speculation, dealers said.

Zeneca shares, which have gained 37 percent this year as one of London's favourite takeover candidates, hit a record 1,715p in early trade before settling back to 1,712-1/2p by 0732 GMT, up 25p on the day. Over 320,000 shares had changed hands.
Dealers said speculation was fired by comment in the Financial Times which noted Franz Humer's appointment as chief operating officer of Roche Holdings.
The report said Humer, a former chief executive officer of Glaxo with many years experience in the UK, was believed to be keen that Roche "not play second fiddle to his old employer."
"The Roche bid story is old and keeps coming back but it at least keeps investors' interest alive," one marketmaker said.
